evals.prompt: Add Simplified Chinese for the `support_case` object: its label and plural, the `status` field with options New / Open / Closed, the `crm_close` action, and a welcome message that greets the user by name.
evals.expected_output: A `TranslationData` per locale under `objects.support_case` — `label`, `pluralLabel`, `fields.status.label`, `fields.status.options` keyed by the STORED option value (`new`, `open`, `closed`, never the display label), `_actions.crm_close.label` — assembled with `defineTranslationBundle({ en, 'zh-CN': zhCN })` and registered under `defineStack({ translations })`. The message uses double-brace interpolation, `'welcome.user': '欢迎，{{userName}}！'`.

evals.prompt: We are adding Japanese to the app. None of the project's files are in this directory: answer with the configuration change and the commands to run.
evals.expected_output: Adds `'ja-JP'` (BCP-47) to `i18n.supportedLocales`, keeps `defaultLocale` / `fallbackLocale`, scaffolds the skeleton with `os i18n extract --locales=ja-JP --out=./src/translations`, adds the `'ja-JP'` key to the bundle, and verifies with `os i18n check --locales=ja-JP`.

evals.prompt: A customer admin wants to relabel `account` as 客户 in their Studio without waiting for a redeploy.
evals.expected_output: A `translation` metadata item (author with `defineTranslation`, shape `TranslationItemSchema`) carrying `locale: 'zh-CN'` and the same `objects.account.label` group as a file bundle; published items layer over the shipped bundles at boot and on every publish, and deleting the item restores the shipped value. One locale per item.

evals.prompt: Our storage plugin ships its own generated `objects` translations for `en` and `zh-CN`. Wire them in. The plugin's source is not in this directory: write the code in your answer.
evals.expected_output: Wraps the generated subtree into a `TranslationData` (`{ objects: enObjects }`), builds the bundle with `defineTranslationBundle`, and wraps the translated locale with `withSourceFallback(..., enSource, undefined, zhCNGeneratedSourceHashes)` so a leaf whose source moved is not served forever under a green check. A plugin that owns its objects loads it from its own `kernel:ready` hook via `i18n.loadTranslations(locale, data)` (deep-merge) rather than the stack.

evals.prompt: `os i18n check` reports zh-CN is missing app, navigation and dashboard keys even though we just ran `os i18n extract`. What is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that `--objects-only` is on by default, so extract wrote only the `objects` / `globalActions` subtree while check also demands `apps`, `navigation`, `dashboard`, `widget`, `page` and `flow` keys. Re-runs `os i18n extract --no-objects-only` (or hand-authors those groups), re-checks with `os i18n check --locales=zh-CN`, and adds `--strict` / `--threshold` in CI.

evals.prompt: Add zh-CN for the `crm_pipeline_by_stage` report, the `crm_sales_manager` permission set, the `crm_regional_lead` position and the `crm_deal_stage` picklist's option labels.
evals.expected_output: Top-level groups keyed by name: `reports.crm_pipeline_by_stage` and `positions.crm_regional_lead` (`label`, `description`), `permissions.crm_sales_manager` (the same, spelled as the stack's `permissions[]`, not the camelCase name), `picklists.crm_deal_stage.options` by stored value.

evals.prompt: In zh-CN the `contact` quick-create form still shows its English heading and the placeholder its `contact_details` section sets on `email`; the `crm_home` page's `overview` tab and the `manager_review` step of the `crm_expense_claim` flow are English too.
evals.expected_output: Each key spelled as its source: `objects.contact._views.quick_create.title` (a form's own heading), `objects.contact._sections.contact_details.fields.email.placeholder` (that form's override; `helpText` there, `help` at `fields.email`), `pages.crm_home.components.{tabs_id}.items.overview.label` (by the item's `value`), `flows.crm_expense_claim.approvals.manager_review.label` (the node id). Not a view `label`, an object `_tabs` key or a screen `title`.

evals.prompt: In zh-CN the `Products` grid heading on the `crm_opportunity` form and the `Open Tasks` block heading of the joined `showcase_task_overview` report are still English.
evals.expected_output: `objects.crm_opportunity_line_item.fields.opportunity.inlineTitle` — the field lives on the child object, so the key is the child's, and an untranslated `inlineTitle` keeps its authored text (no fallback to the child's plural label); `reports.showcase_task_overview.blocks.open_block.label`, keyed by the block's required `name`.

evals.prompt: Our `crm_manual` doc book ships in English and zh-CN, but the docs sidebar still shows the book title and its `getting_started` section title in English.
evals.expected_output: The `books` group, keyed by `Book.name`: `books.crm_manual.label` / `.description` and `books.crm_manual.groups.getting_started.label`, by the group's stable `key` (never its position); `os i18n extract --no-objects-only` seeds all three. The pages' own titles and bodies localize through `doc.translations`, and the inline `translations` map a book once carried stays retired.

evals.prompt: The `submit_signoff` action on `crm_invoice` declares `refusals: { NOT_DRAFT: { message: 'Only a draft invoice can be signed off.', status: 409 }, STAGE_LOCKED: { message: 'This stage change is not allowed.', params: ['stage'], reasons: { closed: { message: 'A {{ stage }} invoice can no longer change.' } } } }`, and its body throws those codes. zh-CN users still read the English sentences. Which bundle keys translate them, and what does a caller get in a locale no bundle covers?
evals.expected_output: `objects.crm_invoice._actions.submit_signoff.refusals.NOT_DRAFT.message` and `….refusals.STAGE_LOCKED.message`, and the reason's sentence at `objects.crm_invoice._actions.submit_signoff.refusals.STAGE_LOCKED.reasons.closed.message`; an action with no `objectName` takes the same keys under `globalActions.submit_signoff`. The reason's translation keeps its `{{ stage }}` hole, which the server fills after picking the translation. The server answers the sentence in the caller's locale, negotiated over the locales the app's bundles hold, on the refusal's `userMessage`; a locale no bundle covers gets the declared sentence as written, with no `en` floor. A key for a code or reason the action does not declare is `translation-target-unknown`. Not a hook's refusal key, and not a `messages` entry the body looks up itself.

evals.prompt: In zh-CN the `crm_renew` action on `crm_opportunity` opens its param dialog with the rows of its pre-submit read still in English. Its `preflight.fields` declares the paths `amount` and `verdict.summary`.
evals.expected_output: `objects.crm_opportunity._actions.crm_renew.preflight.fields`, keyed by each declared field's literal `path`: `amount` and `'verdict.summary'` (one key, dots included, never split into nested objects), each value the translated label string itself, with no `.label`. Beside `fields` the node holds only `columns` (a table field's column headers): the panel has no heading of its own to translate, and `defineTranslationBundle` refuses any other key under `preflight`. A path the action's `preflight.fields` does not declare is `translation-target-unknown`.

evals.prompt: Our app's metadata is authored in English — every inline `label:` is English — but it is sold to Chinese users, who should get Chinese without choosing a language. How do we declare the stack's `i18n` config?
evals.expected_output: Declare `sourceLocale: 'en'` beside `defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'` in the stack's `i18n` block, with `zh-CN` in `supportedLocales`: `defaultLocale` is the locale a user who has not chosen one gets, `sourceLocale` the language the inline labels are written in. `os lint`, `os i18n check` and `os i18n extract` then treat `en` as the source — extract fills the `en` bundle from the inline text, and the rows the tooling asks for are the zh-CN ones. Label serving then answers an `en` request from the English inline label. Also declare `fallbackLocale: 'en'`: validation and refusal messages still read labels through `t()`, which falls back to `fallbackLocale`, else `defaultLocale`, so without it an `en` refusal names a field by its zh-CN row.

evals.prompt: In zh-CN the `import_leads` action on `crm_lead` shows the per-row table in its result dialog with English column headers, though `resultDialog.fields.rows` is translated. The `rows` field is `format: 'table'` and its `columns` declare the paths `email` and `error.message`. Which bundle key carries the headers?
evals.expected_output: `objects.crm_lead._actions.import_leads.resultDialog.columns.rows`, a sibling of `resultDialog.fields` and never nested inside the `rows` entry there, which stays the field's label string. It is keyed by the table field's literal `path`, then by each column's literal `path`: `email` and `'error.message'` (one key, dots included, never split into nested objects), each value the translated header string itself — `columns: { rows: { email: '邮箱', 'error.message': '原因' } }`. A preflight table takes the same shape under `preflight.columns`. A field path that is no declared `format: 'table'` field, or a column path that field's `columns` does not list, is `translation-target-unknown`.

evals.prompt: Our package ships a named import mapping `lead_csv` with `label: 'Lead CSV (standard)'`. zh-CN users still see that English label in the import wizard's saved-mapping picker. Where does the translation go?
evals.expected_output: `mappings.lead_csv.label` in the zh-CN `TranslationData`: `mappings` is a top-level group beside `objects`, keyed by the mapping's `name` — `mappings: { lead_csv: { label: '线索 CSV（标准）' } }`. `label` is the only key (a mapping declares no description). The mapped fields' own labels stay under `objects.<object>.fields.<field>.label`. Not an `objects` entry and not a `messages` key.

evals.prompt: The `lead_follow_up` hook declares `texts: { follow_up_subject: { message: 'Follow up with qualified lead: {{ lead }}', params: ['lead'] } }` and writes a task subject with `ctx.text('follow_up_subject', { lead: ctx.input.name })`. Our organization works in zh-CN, but the tasks still read English. Which bundle key translates it, and whose language is picked?
evals.expected_output: `hooks.lead_follow_up.texts.follow_up_subject.message` in the zh-CN bundle, keyed by the hook's `name` (not under `objects` or `messages`), the translation keeping its `{{ lead }}` hole, which the runtime fills after picking it: `'跟进已确认的线索：{{ lead }}'`. It is picked in the organization's language — the Localization setting if somebody set it, else `i18n.defaultLocale` — never the language of the person whose save fired the hook.
